subject: Anatomy
stem: A 74-year-old man is brought to the clinic by his daughter because of gradual cognitive decline, urinary incontinence, and difficulty walking over the past 8 months. His daughter notes that he has become increasingly forgetful, slow to respond, and has had several episodes of involuntary urination before reaching the toilet. On physical examination, his gait is slow, wide-based, and shuffling, with his feet appearing 'glued to the floor' (magnetic gait); however, there is no resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, or extremity weakness. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ symmetrically, and plantar responses are flexor. Non-contrast head CT reveals marked symmetric enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles out of proportion to sulcal enlargement, with flattening of cortical sulci against the calvarium. Lumbar puncture demonstrates a normal opening pressure of 130 mm H2O; removal of 35 mL of cerebrospinal fluid leads to immediate, marked improvement in his gait velocity and step height. Which of the following neuroanatomical mechanisms directly explains the patient's gait disturbance and urinary urgency?

options.text: Selective neurodegeneration of pigmented dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta
options.explanation: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta causes Parkinson disease, presenting with asymmetric resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability, rather than the isolated magnetic gait, ventriculomegaly, and CSF tap test responsiveness of NPH.

options.text: Ischemic demyelination of the posterior columns in the cervical spinal cord
options.explanation: Dorsal column demyelination (as seen in subacute combined degeneration or tabes dorsalis) causes sensory ataxia with positive Romberg sign and loss of vibratory/proprioceptive sensation, not a frontal/magnetic gait apraxia.

options.text: Stretching of sacral and lower extremity corticospinal fibers in the corona radiata
options.explanation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) is characterized by the classic triad of gait disturbance ('magnetic' gait / gait apraxia), cognitive impairment, and urinary urge incontinence ('wet, wacky, and wobbly'). Ventriculomegaly with normal opening pressure exerts mechanical shear stress and distention on the periventricular white matter, specifically stretching the corona radiata fibers traversing alongside the lateral ventricles. Because the sacral and lumbar motor and autonomic fibers course most medially adjacent to the ventricular wall, they are stretched first, causing lower extremity gait disturbance and early urinary urge incontinence.

options.text: Atrophy of cholinergic neurons within the nucleus basalis of Meynert
options.explanation: Nucleus basalis of Meynert degeneration is prominent in Alzheimer disease, which causes early profound episodic memory impairment rather than prominent early gait apraxia and urinary urgency with ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal widening.

options.text: Obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid outflow at the bilateral foramina of Monro
options.explanation: Obstruction at the foramina of Monro causes non-communicating (obstructive) hydrocephalus of the lateral ventricles with elevated intracranial pressure (headache, papilledema, vomiting), not normal-pressure communicating hydrocephalus with the clinical triad.

explanation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) is characterized by the classic triad of gait disturbance ('magnetic' gait / gait apraxia), cognitive impairment, and urinary urge incontinence ('wet, wacky, and wobbly'). Ventriculomegaly with normal opening pressure exerts mechanical shear stress and distention on the periventricular white matter, specifically stretching the corona radiata fibers traversing alongside the lateral ventricles. Because the sacral and lumbar motor and autonomic fibers course most medially adjacent to the ventricular wall, they are stretched first, causing lower extremity gait disturbance and early urinary urge incontinence. Magnetic gait + cognitive decline + urinary incontinence ('wet, wacky, wobbly') + ventriculomegaly + CSF tap improvement -> NPH (stretching of sacral motor fibers in corona radiata).
